metadata.title: Global-in-time smoothing effects for Schrödinger equations with inverse-square potentials

nodes.name: Inhomogeneous Schrödinger equation with potential
nodes.statement: i\partial_t u(t,x)=Hu(t,x)+F(t,x);\quad u(0,x)=\psi(x),

nodes.name: Global-in-time smoothing effect for the free Schrödinger equation
nodes.statement: It is well-known that the solution $u=e^{it\Delta}\psi$ to the free Schr\"odinger equation $$ i\partial_t u(t,x)=-\Delta u(t,x);\quad u|_{t=0}=\psi\in L^2(\R^n), $$ satisfies the following global-in-time smoothing effect \begin{align} \norm{\<x\>^{-\rho}|D|^{1/2}e^{it\Delta}\psi}_{L^2(\R^{1+n})}\le C\norm{\psi}_{L^2(\R^n)}, \end{align} where $\<x\>=(1+|x|^2)^{1/2}$, $\rho>1/2$ and $|D|=(-\Delta)^{1/2}$ (see Ben-Artzi and Klainerman \cite{BeKl} for $n\ge3$ and Chihara \cite{Chi} for $n=2$).
nodes.statement_short: Free Schrödinger solutions gain half a derivative in the weighted space-time $L^2$ norm.
assumptions: the solution $u=e^{it\Delta}\psi$ to the free Schr\"odinger equation $$ i\partial_t u(t,x)=-\Delta u(t,x);\quad u|_{t=0}=\psi\in L^2(\R^n), $$

nodes.name: Kato–Yajima smoothing estimate
nodes.statement_short: An $L^n$ weight controls the space-time $L^2$ norm of the free evolution.

nodes.name: Endpoint Strichartz estimate
nodes.statement: The estimate \eqref{intro_2} also follows from H\"older's inequality and the endpoint Strichartz estimate proved by Keel and Tao \cite{KeTa}: \begin{align} \norm{e^{it\Delta}\psi}_{L^2(\R;L^{\frac{2n}{n-2}}(\R^n))}\le C\norm{\psi}_{L^2(\R^n)}, \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The free evolution maps $L^2$ data into $L^2_tL^{2n/(n-2)}_x$.

nodes.name: Schrödinger operator with inverse-square potential $H_a$
nodes.statement: the Schr\"odinger operator with the inverse-square potential of the form\ $$ H_a=-\Delta+a|x|^{-2},\quad a>-\frac{(n-2)^2}{4}, $$

nodes.name: Hardy's inequality
nodes.statement: $(n-2)^2/4$ is the best constant in Hardy's inequality \begin{align} \frac{(n-2)^2}{4}\int |x|^{-2}|u|^2dx\le \int|\nabla u|^2dx,\quad u\in C_0^\infty(\R^n). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $(n-2)^2/4$ is the sharp constant in the inverse-square/gradient $L^2$ inequality.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1 (smoothing effect for $H_a$ with $a\ge-(n-2)^2/4+1/4$)
nodes.statement: Let $n\ge3$, $a\ge -(n-2)^2/4+1/4$ and $\ep>0$. Then there exists $C_\ep>0$ such that for all $\psi\in L^2(\R^n)$, $e^{-itH_a}\psi$ satisfies \begin{align} \norm{w(|x|)|D|^{1/2}e^{-itH_a}\psi}_{L^2(\R^{1+n})}\le C_\ep\norm{\psi}_{L^2(\R^n)} \end{align} where $w(r)=r^{(\ep-1)/2}(1+r^\ep)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: For $a\ge-(n-2)^2/4+1/4$ the half-derivative smoothing estimate holds for $e^{-itH_a}$ with weight $w$.

nodes.name: Two-sided weighted norm equivalence for $H_a^{s/2}$
nodes.statement:
The condition $a\ge -(n-2)^2/4+1/4$ was used to ensure that $w$ satisfies some conditions for two-sided weighted norm estimates $$C_1
orm{w(x)(-\Delta)^{s/2}f}_{L^2}\le 
orm{w(x)H_a^{s/2}f}_{L^2}\le C_2 
orm{w(x)(-\Delta)^{s/2}f}_{L^2}$$ established by the same paper (see \cite[Theorem 1.1]{BDDLL}).
nodes.statement_short: Weighted $L^2$ norms of $H_a^{s/2}f$ and $(-\Delta)^{s/2}f$ are comparable under the stated condition on $a$.

nodes.name: Does the smoothing estimate hold for all $a>-(n-2)^2/4$?
nodes.statement: Then authors raised a question whether \eqref{theorem_BDDLL_1} holds under the condition $a>-(n-2)^2/4$.
nodes.statement_short: Whether the smoothing estimate extends to all $a>-(n-2)^2/4$.

nodes.name: Assumption A (conditions on the potential $V$)
nodes.statement_short: $V$ is real-valued with $|x|V\in L^{n,\infty}$, $x\cdot\nabla V\in L^{n/2,\infty}$, and both $-\Delta+V$ and $-\Delta-V-x\cdot\nabla V$ dominate $-\delta\Delta$ in the form sense.

nodes.name: Inverse-square potential as an admissible $V$
nodes.statement: A typical example satisfying Assumption \ref{assumption_A} is the inverse-square potential $V(x)=a|x|^{-2}$ with $a>-(n-2)^2/4$. In this case, it follows from Hardy's inequality \eqref{Hardy} that \eqref{assumption_A_1} is satisfied with $\delta=1-4|a|/(n-2)^2>0$ if $a<0$ or $\delta=1$ if $a\ge0$.
nodes.statement_short: $V=a|x|^{-2}$ with $a>-(n-2)^2/4$ satisfies Assumption A, with $\delta$ computed from Hardy's inequality.

nodes.name: Admissible potential with $|x|^2V\notin L^\infty$
nodes.statement: Moreover, Assumption \ref{assumption_A} is general enough to include some potentials such that $|x|^2V\notin L^\infty$. For instance, we let $c_1,c_2>0$, $\alpha\in\R^n$ and $\chi\in C^1(\R)$ such that $0\le \chi\le 1$ and $|\chi^{(k)}(t)|\le |t|^{-k-1}$ for $|t|\ge1$. Then $$ V(x)=\frac{-(n-2)^2/4+c_1}{|x|^{2}}-\frac{c_2\chi(|x-\alpha|)}{|x-\alpha|} $$ satisfies Assumption \ref{assumption_A} with $\delta=c_1-c_2(2+\sup|\chi'|)(|\alpha|+1)$ if $$ 0<c_2<\frac{c_1}{(2+\sup|\chi'|)(|\alpha|+1)}. $$
nodes.statement_short: A sum of a critical inverse-square term and a Coulomb-type bump satisfies Assumption A for small $c_2$.

nodes.name: Closability of the quadratic form $Q_H$
nodes.statement: Under Assumption \ref{assumption_A}, Hardy's inequality \eqref{Hardy} implies that the sesquilinear form $$Q_H(u,v)=\<(-\Delta+V)u,v\> ,\quad u,v\in C_0^\infty(\R^n),$$ is symmetric, non-negative and closable such that the domain of its closure $\overline{Q}_H$ satisfies $D(\overline{Q}_H)=\mathcal H^1(\R^n)$.
nodes.statement_short: $Q_H$ is symmetric, non-negative and closable with form domain $\mathcal H^1(\R^n)$.
conclusions: is symmetric, non-negative and closable such that the domain of its closure $\overline{Q}_H$ satisfies $D(\overline{Q}_H)=\mathcal H^1(\R^n)$

nodes.name: Friedrichs extension $H$, propagator $e^{-itH}$ and inhomogeneous propagator $\Gamma_H$
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be the Friedrichs extension of $\overline Q_H$, $e^{-itH}$ the unitary group on $L^2(\R^n)$ generated by $H$ via Stone's theorem and $\Gamma_H$ the inhomogeneous propagator defined by \begin{align} \Gamma_HF(t)=\int_0^t e^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds,\quad F\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R;L^2(\R^n)). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $H$ is the Friedrichs extension of $\overline Q_H$, $e^{-itH}$ its unitary group, and $\Gamma_H$ the Duhamel operator.

nodes.name: Duhamel representation of the unique mild solution
nodes.statement: Then a unique (mild) solution to the Schr\"odinger equation \eqref{equation} is given by \begin{align} u(t)=e^{-itH}\psi-i\Gamma_HF(t). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The mild solution of the inhomogeneous problem is $u=e^{-itH}\psi-i\Gamma_HF$.

nodes.name: Muckenhoupt $A_2$ class
nodes.statement: We say that $v(x)$ belongs to the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ class if $v,1/v\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^n)$, $v\ge0$ and $$ \Big(\frac{1}{|B|}\int_B v(x)dx\Big)\Big(\frac{1}{|B|}\int_{B}\frac{1}{v(x)}dx\Big)\le C $$ for all ball $B\subset \R^n$ with some constant $C>0$ independent of $B$.
nodes.statement_short: A weight $v$ is $A_2$ if the product of the averages of $v$ and $1/v$ over any ball is uniformly bounded.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2 (main global-in-time smoothing effect)
nodes.statement:
Let $n\ge3$, $V$ satisfy Assumption ef{assumption_A} and $w\in L^2(\R)$. Suppose $w(|x|)^2\in A_2$ and, for any $j=1,2,...,n$, there exists $C_j>0$ such that $$ w(|x|)\le C_jw(x_j),\quad x=(x_1,...,x_n)\in \R^n. $$ Then there exists $C>0$, independent of $w$, such that $e^{-itH}$ satisfies $$ 
orm{w(|x|)|D|^{1/2}e^{-itH}\psi}_{L^{2}(\R^{1+n})}\le C
orm{w}_{L^2(\R)}
orm{\psi}_{L^2(\R^n)},\quad \psi\in L^2(\R^n). $$
nodes.statement_short: For $A_2$-admissible radial weights $w$, $e^{-itH}$ satisfies the half-derivative weighted smoothing estimate with constant $C\norm{w}_{L^2}$.
assumptions: Suppose $w(|x|)^2\in A_2$ and, for any $j=1,2,...,n$, there exists $C_j>0$ such that $$ w(|x|)\le C_jw(x_j),\quad x=(x_1,...,x_n)\in \R^n. $$
conclusions:
Then there exists $C>0$, independent of $w$, such that $e^{-itH}$ satisfies $$ 
orm{w(|x|)|D|^{1/2}e^{-itH}\psi}_{L^{2}(\R^{1+n})}\le C
orm{w}_{L^2(\R)}
orm{\psi}_{L^2(\R^n)},\quad \psi\in L^2(\R^n). $$

nodes.name: Admissible weight $w(r)=r^{(\ep-1)/2}(1+r^\ep)^{-1}$
nodes.statement: Assuming $0<\ep<1$ without loss of generality, it is easy to see that $w(r)=r^{(\ep-1)/2}(1+r^\ep)^{-1}$ fulfills the above conditions.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3 (smoothing and Strichartz estimates with $\<x\>^{-\rho}$ weights)
nodes.statement:
Let $n\ge3$, $ho>1/2$ and $\A,\B\in \{\dot\H^{-1/2,ho}(\R^n),\ L^{ rac{2n}{n+2},2}(\R^n)\}$. Suppose $V$ satisfies Assumption ef{assumption_A}. Then the solution $u$ to \eqref{equation} given by \eqref{solution} satisfies  egin{align} 
orm{u}_{L^{2}(\R;\B^*)}\le C
orm{\psi}_{L^2(\R^n)}+C
orm{F}_{L^2(\R;\A)} \end{align} for all $\psi\in L^2(\R^n)$ and $F\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R;L^2(\R^n)) \cap L^2(\R;\A)$.
nodes.statement_short: The solution of the inhomogeneous problem is bounded in $L^2_t\B^*$ by the data, for any mix of the weighted-Sobolev and Lorentz endpoint spaces.
assumptions: for all $\psi\in L^2(\R^n)$ and $F\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R;L^2(\R^n)) \cap L^2(\R;\A)$

nodes.name: Weighted homogeneous Sobolev space $\dot\H^{s,\mu}(\R^n)$
nodes.statement: Here $\dot\H^{s,\mu}(\R^n)$ denotes the weighted homogeneous Sobolev space equipped with the norm $\norm{f}_{\dot\H^{s,\mu}}=\norm{\<x\>^{\mu}|D|^{s}f}_{L^2}$.

nodes.name: Duality of $\A,\B$ and novelty of Theorem 1.3
nodes.statement: Note that $(L^{\frac{2n}{n+2},2}(\R^n))^*=L^{\frac{2n}{n-2},2}(\R^n)$ and $(\dot\H^{-1/2,\rho}(\R^n))^*=\dot\H^{1/2,-\rho}(\R^n)$. If $\A=\B=L^{\frac{2n}{n+2},2}(\R^n)$, \eqref{theorem_2_1} becomes the endpoint Strichartz estimate and was proved by our previous work \cite{BoMi}. If $\A=\B=\dot\H^{-1/2,\rho}(\R^n)$, \eqref{theorem_2_1} is a generalization of \eqref{intro_1} and seems to be new under Assumption \ref{assumption_A}. Here we stress that $\A$ and $\B$ do not have to coincide.
nodes.statement_short: Diagonal choices recover the endpoint Strichartz estimate and a generalization of the free smoothing estimate; the off-diagonal case is the new content.

nodes.name: Time-truncated Bochner norm $\norm{F}_{L^p_T\X}$
nodes.statement: For $T>0$ and a Banach space $\X$, we denote $\norm{F}_{L^p_T\X}=\norm{F}_{L^p([-T,T];\X)}$.

nodes.name: Lorentz space $L^{p,q}(\R^n)$
nodes.statement:
$L^{p,q}(\R^n)$ denotes the Lorentz space equipped with the norm $
orm{\cdot}_{L^{p,q}(\R^n)}$ satisfying $
orm{f}_{L^{p,q}(\R^n)}\sim
orm{t d_f(t)^{1/p}}_{L^q(\R_+,t^{-1}dt)}$, where $d_f(t):=\mu(\{x\in \R^n\ |\ |f(x)|>t\})$ is the distribution function of $f$.
nodes.statement_short: The Lorentz norm is the $L^q(\R_+,t^{-1}dt)$ norm of $t\,d_f(t)^{1/p}$, with $d_f$ the distribution function.

nodes.name: Hölder's inequality for Lorentz spaces
Sobolev's inequality in Lorentz spaces
$H$-smooth operator (Kato)
nodes.statement: Then we say that $A$ is {\it $H$-smooth} with bound $a$ if $$ \sup_{z\in \C\setminus\R}|\<(R_H(z)-R_H(\overline z))A^*\psi,A^*\psi\>|\le \frac{a^2}{2}\norm{\psi}^2,\quad \psi\in D(A^*). $$

nodes.name: $H$-supersmooth operator
nodes.statement: We say that $A$ is {\it $H$-supersmooth} with bound $a$ if $$ \sup_{z\in \C\setminus\R}|\<R_H(z)A^*\psi,A^*\psi\>|\le \frac{a}{2}\norm{\psi}^2,\quad \psi\in D(A^*). $$

nodes.name: Supersmoothness implies smoothness
nodes.statement: Note that if $A$ is $H$-supersmooth with bound $a$ then $A$ is $H$-smooth with bound $(2a)^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.1 (smoothness ↔ space-time estimates)
nodes.statement:
{m (1)} $A$ is $H$-smooth with bound $a$ if and only if, for any $\psi\in \H$, $e^{-itH}\psi$ belongs to $D(A)$ for a.e. $t\in \R$ and  egin{align} 
orm{Ae^{-itH}\psi}_{L^2(\R;\H)} \le a
orm{\psi}. \end{align} {m (2)} Suppose $A$ is $H$-supersmooth with bound $a$. Then, for any simple function $F:\R	o D(A^*)$ and $t\in \R$, $Ae^{-i(t-s)H}A^*F(s)$ is Bochner integrable in $s$ over $[0,t]$ (or $[t,0]$) and satisfies  egin{align}  ignorm{e^{-|\ep t|}\int_0^t Ae^{-i(t-s)H}A^*F(s)ds}_{L^2(\R;\H)}\le a
orm{e^{-|\ep t|}F}_{L^2(\R;\H)} \end{align} for all $\ep\in \R$. Conversely, if the estimate \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_2} holds for all simple function $F:\R	o D(A^*)$ and $|\ep|<\ep_0$ with some $\ep_0>0$, then $A$ is $H$-supersmooth with bound $a$.
nodes.statement_short: $H$-smoothness is equivalent to the homogeneous space-time bound; supersmoothness is equivalent to the corresponding inhomogeneous (Duhamel) bound.
conclusions: $A$ is $H$-smooth with bound $a$ if and only if, for any $\psi\in \H$, $e^{-itH}\psi$ belongs to $D(A)$ for a.e. $t\in \R$ and \begin{align} \norm{Ae^{-itH}\psi}_{L^2(\R;\H)} \le a\norm{\psi}. \end{align}

$Ae^{-i(t-s)H}A^*F(s)$ is Bochner integrable in $s$ over $[0,t]$ (or $[t,0]$) and satisfies \begin{align} \bignorm{e^{-|\ep t|}\int_0^t Ae^{-i(t-s)H}A^*F(s)ds}_{L^2(\R;\H)}\le a\norm{e^{-|\ep t|}F}_{L^2(\R;\H)} \end{align} for all $\ep\in \R$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.1
nodes.statement: The first statement is due to \cite[Lemma 3.6 and Theorem 5.1]{Kat} (see also \cite[Theorem XIII.25]{ReSi}). The second assertion was proved by \cite[Theorem 2.3]{Dan}.
nodes.statement_short: Both assertions are quoted from the literature: Kato for part (1), D'Ancona for part (2).

nodes.name: Cite Kato for part (1)
nodes.statement: The first statement is due to \cite[Lemma 3.6 and Theorem 5.1]{Kat} (see also \cite[Theorem XIII.25]{ReSi}).
nodes.statement_short: Invoke Kato's characterization of $H$-smoothness.

nodes.name: Cite D'Ancona for part (2)
nodes.statement: The second assertion was proved by \cite[Theorem 2.3]{Dan}.
nodes.statement_short: Invoke D'Ancona's inhomogeneous supersmoothness theorem.

nodes.name: $H$-smooth operators are infinitesimally $H$-bounded
nodes.statement: Note that if $A$ is $H$-smooth then $A$ is infinitesimally $H$-bounded (\cite[Theorem XIII.22]{ReSi}).

nodes.name: Time-truncated form of the supersmoothness estimate
nodes.statement: Also note that the estimate \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_2} can be replaced by \begin{align} \bignorm{e^{-|\ep t|}\int_0^t Ae^{-i(t-s)H}A^*F(s)ds}_{L^2_T\H}\le a\norm{e^{-|\ep t|}F}_{L^2_T\H}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The Duhamel bound of Proposition 2.1(2) may equivalently be stated on the time interval $[-T,T]$.

nodes.name: Proof that the truncated estimate is equivalent
nodes.statement: Indeed, \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_2} implies \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_3} since $s\in [-T,T]$ if $t\in[-T,T]$ and $s\in[0,t]$ (or $s\in [-t,0]$). Conversely, since \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_3} implies $$ \bignorm{e^{-|\ep t|}\int_0^t Ae^{-i(t-s)H}A^*F(s)ds}_{L^2_T\H}\le a\norm{e^{-|\ep t|}F}_{L^2(\R;\H)} $$ and $a$ is independent of $T$, one has \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_2} by letting $T\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Restriction gives one implication; letting $T\to\infty$ in the $T$-uniform bound gives the converse.

nodes.name: Forward implication by restriction
nodes.statement: Indeed, \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_2} implies \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_3} since $s\in [-T,T]$ if $t\in[-T,T]$ and $s\in[0,t]$ (or $s\in [-t,0]$).
nodes.statement_short: Restrict the global estimate to $[-T,T]$.

nodes.name: Converse by letting $T\to\infty$
nodes.statement: Conversely, since \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_3} implies $$ \bignorm{e^{-|\ep t|}\int_0^t Ae^{-i(t-s)H}A^*F(s)ds}_{L^2_T\H}\le a\norm{e^{-|\ep t|}F}_{L^2(\R;\H)} $$ and $a$ is independent of $T$, one has \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_2} by letting $T\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Use $T$-independence of $a$ and pass to the limit $T\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Adjoint inhomogeneous propagator $\Gamma_H^*$
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma_H$ be the inhomogeneous propagator defined by the formula \eqref{inhomogeneous_propagator} and set \begin{align} \Gamma_H^*F(t)=\mathds1_{[0,\infty)}(t)\int _t^Te^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds-\mathds1_{(-\infty,0]}(t)\int_{-T}^te^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\Gamma_H^*$ integrates forward from $t$ to $T$ for $t\ge0$ and backward from $-T$ to $t$ for $t\le0$.

nodes.name: $\Gamma_H^*$ is the adjoint of $\Gamma_H$ in $L^2_T\H$
nodes.statement: By a direct calculation, $\<\<\Gamma_HF,G\>\>_T=\<\<F,\Gamma_H^*G\>\>_T$ for $F,G\in L^1_{\loc}\H$, where $$ \<\<F,G\>\>_T:=\int_{-T}^T\<F(t),G(t)\>dt. $$ Hence $\Gamma_H^*$ is the adjoint of $\Gamma_H$ in $L^2_T\H$.
conclusions: Hence $\Gamma_H^*$ is the adjoint of $\Gamma_H$ in $L^2_T\H$.

nodes.name: A priori well-definedness of $A\Gamma_H$ and $A\Gamma_H^*$
nodes.statement:
These operators are a priori well-defined on $L^1_{\loc}(\R;D(H))$ since, for some $z
otin \sigma(H)$ and each $T>0$, $$ 
orm{A\Gamma_HF}_{L^2_T\H}+
orm{A\Gamma^*_HF}_{L^2_T\H}\le C_T
orm{AR_0(z)}_{\mathbb B(\H)}
orm{R_0(z)F}_{L^1_T\H}<\infty $$
nodes.statement_short: Factoring through the resolvent gives a crude finite bound, so $A\Gamma_H$ and $A\Gamma_H^*$ make sense on $L^1_{\loc}(\R;D(H))$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.2 (bounded extension of $A\Gamma_H$, $A\Gamma_H^*$)
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $A$ is $H$-smooth with bound $a$. Then $A\Gamma_H$ and $A\Gamma^*_H$ extend to bounded operators from $L^1_T\H$ to $L^2_T\H$ such that  egin{align} 
orm{A\Gamma_HF}_{L^2_T\H}\le Ca
orm{F}_{L^1_T\H},\quad 
orm{A\Gamma_H^*F}_{L^2_T\H}\le Ca
orm{F}_{L^1_T\H} \end{align} for any $T>0$ and $F\in L^1_T\H$ with some $C>0$ independent of $a,T$ and $F$. Moreover, we have  egin{align} A\Gamma_HF(t)=\int_0^tAe^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds \end{align} for all simple function $F:[-T,T]	o \H$ and a.e. $t\in[-T,T]$. In particular $A\Gamma_HF(t)$ and $\int_0^tAe^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds$ coincide in $L^2_T\H$.
nodes.statement_short: $H$-smoothness of $A$ makes $A\Gamma_H$ and $A\Gamma_H^*$ bounded from $L^1_T\H$ to $L^2_T\H$, with the Duhamel formula valid a.e.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement:
For the sake of self-containedness, we give the proof for $\Gamma_H$ in detail. The proof for $\Gamma_H^*$ is analogous. Let $\chi\in C_0^\infty(\R)$ be such that $\chi\equiv1$ near $0$ and $0\le\chi\le1$ and set $\chi_\ep(t)=\chi(\ep t)$. Note that $A\Gamma_H\chi_\ep(H)=A\chi_\ep(H)\Gamma_H$ is well-defined on $L^1_T\H$ since $A$ is $H$-bounded. Moreover, the $H$-smoothness of $A$ shows$$ ignorm{Ae^{-itH}\int_{[0,T]}e^{isH}\chi_\ep(H)F(s)ds}_{L^2_T\H}\le a
orm{F}_{L^1_T\H}.$$Using the Christ-Kiselev lemma \cite{ChKi}, one can replace $[0,T]$ by $[0,t]$ in the left hand side to obtain$$
orm{A\chi_\ep(H)\Gamma_HF}_{L^2_T\H}\le Ca
orm{F}_{L^1_T\H}$$with some universal constant $C>0$ independent of $F$. This estimate implies that, for all $F\in L^1_T\H$, $A\chi_\ep(H)\Gamma_HF$ converges in $L^2_T\H$ as $\ep	o0$ and the limit denoted by the same symbol $A\Gamma_HF$ satisfies the first estimate in \eqref{lemma_abstract_2_1}. This proves the half part of this lemma. Next, let $F:[-T,T]	o \H$ be a simple function. As we have shown, $A\chi_{\ep_n}(H)\Gamma_H$ converges to $A\Gamma_HF$ in $L^2_T\H$ as $n	o\infty$ for any sequence $\ep_n>0$ with $\ep_n	o0$. Then one can find a subsequence $\ep_{n_k}$ and a null set $\mathcal N\subset [-T,T]$ such that $A\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H)\Gamma_HF	o A\Gamma_HF(t)$ in $\H$ as $k	o\infty$ for all $t\in [-T,T]\setminus \mathcal N$. Hence, in order to show \eqref{lemma_abstract_2_2}, it suffices to check that $$  ignorm{\int_0^tAe^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds-A\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H)\Gamma_HF(t)}_\H	o0 $$ as $k	o\infty$ for all $t\in [-T,T]\setminus \mathcal N$. Let us write $F=\sum_{j=1}^N\mathds1_{E_j}(t)f_j$ with $f_j\in \H$ and measurable sets $E_j\subset [-T,T]$. Then we have for all $t\in [-T,T]\setminus \mathcal N$,  egin{align*} & ignorm{\int_0^tAe^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds-A\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H)\Gamma_HF(t)}_\H\ &\le \sum_{j=1}^N ignorm{\int_{[0,t]\cap M_j}Ae^{isH}(1-\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H))e^{-itH}f_jds}_\H\ &\le \sum_{j=1}^NT^{1/2}\Big(\int_\R
orm{Ae^{isH}e^{-itH}(1-\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H))f_j}_{\H}^2ds\Big)^{1/2}\ &\le CT^{1/2}\sum_{j=1}^N
orm{(1-\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H))f_j}_{\H}	o 0 \end{align*} as $k	o\infty$, where we have used H"older's inequality in the third line and the $H$-smoothness of $A$ and the unitarity of $e^{-itH}$ in the last line. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Regularize with $\chi_\ep(H)$, apply the Christ–Kiselev lemma to pass from $[0,T]$ to $[0,t]$, then identify the limit along a subsequence.

nodes.name: Regularizing cut-off $\chi_\ep(H)$
nodes.statement: For the sake of self-containedness, we give the proof for $\Gamma_H$ in detail. The proof for $\Gamma_H^*$ is analogous. Let $\chi\in C_0^\infty(\R)$ be such that $\chi\equiv1$ near $0$ and $0\le\chi\le1$ and set $\chi_\ep(t)=\chi(\ep t)$. Note that $A\Gamma_H\chi_\ep(H)=A\chi_\ep(H)\Gamma_H$ is well-defined on $L^1_T\H$ since $A$ is $H$-bounded.
nodes.statement_short: Set up a smooth spectral cut-off $\chi_\ep(H)$ that makes the composition well defined.

nodes.name: Christ–Kiselev lemma and the uniform bound
nodes.statement:
Moreover, the $H$-smoothness of $A$ shows$$ ignorm{Ae^{-itH}\int_{[0,T]}e^{isH}\chi_\ep(H)F(s)ds}_{L^2_T\H}\le a
orm{F}_{L^1_T\H}.$$Using the Christ-Kiselev lemma \cite{ChKi}, one can replace $[0,T]$ by $[0,t]$ in the left hand side to obtain$$
orm{A\chi_\ep(H)\Gamma_HF}_{L^2_T\H}\le Ca
orm{F}_{L^1_T\H}$$with some universal constant $C>0$ independent of $F$. This estimate implies that, for all $F\in L^1_T\H$, $A\chi_\ep(H)\Gamma_HF$ converges in $L^2_T\H$ as $\ep	o0$ and the limit denoted by the same symbol $A\Gamma_HF$ satisfies the first estimate in \eqref{lemma_abstract_2_1}. This proves the half part of this lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Christ–Kiselev lemma to replace $[0,T]$ by $[0,t]$ and pass to the limit $\ep\to0$.

nodes.name: Identification of $A\Gamma_HF(t)$ with the Duhamel integral
nodes.statement: Next, let $F:[-T,T]\to \H$ be a simple function. As we have shown, $A\chi_{\ep_n}(H)\Gamma_H$ converges to $A\Gamma_HF$ in $L^2_T\H$ as $n\to\infty$ for any sequence $\ep_n>0$ with $\ep_n\to0$. Then one can find a subsequence $\ep_{n_k}$ and a null set $\mathcal N\subset [-T,T]$ such that $A\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H)\Gamma_HF\to A\Gamma_HF(t)$ in $\H$ as $k\to\infty$ for all $t\in [-T,T]\setminus \mathcal N$. Hence, in order to show \eqref{lemma_abstract_2_2}, it suffices to check that $$ \bignorm{\int_0^tAe^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds-A\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H)\Gamma_HF(t)}_\H\to0 $$ as $k\to\infty$ for all $t\in [-T,T]\setminus \mathcal N$. Let us write $F=\sum_{j=1}^N\mathds1_{E_j}(t)f_j$ with $f_j\in \H$ and measurable sets $E_j\subset [-T,T]$. Then we have for all $t\in [-T,T]\setminus \mathcal N$, \begin{align*} &\bignorm{\int_0^tAe^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds-A\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H)\Gamma_HF(t)}_\H\\ &\le \sum_{j=1}^N\bignorm{\int_{[0,t]\cap M_j}Ae^{isH}(1-\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H))e^{-itH}f_jds}_\H\\ &\le \sum_{j=1}^NT^{1/2}\Big(\int_\R\norm{Ae^{isH}e^{-itH}(1-\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H))f_j}_{\H}^2ds\Big)^{1/2}\\ &\le CT^{1/2}\sum_{j=1}^N\norm{(1-\chi_{\ep_{n_k}}(H))f_j}_{\H}\to 0 \end{align*} as $k\to\infty$, where we have used H\"older's inequality in the third line and the $H$-smoothness of $A$ and the unitarity of $e^{-itH}$ in the last line. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Along a subsequence the regularized operators converge a.e., and the difference tends to zero by Hölder plus $H$-smoothness.

nodes.name: Bound for $A\Gamma_HA^*$ under supersmoothness
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{proposition_abstract_1} (1), \eqref{proposition_abstract_1_3} and this lemma, if $A$ is $H$-supersmooth with bound $a$ then $A\Gamma_HA^*$ is well-defined on $L^1_{\loc}(\R;(D(A^*))$ and satisfies $ \norm{A\Gamma_HA^*F}_{L^2_T\H}\le a\norm{F}_{L^2_T\H} $ for all simple function $F:[-T,T]\to D(A^*)$.
nodes.statement_short: Supersmoothness of $A$ gives $\norm{A\Gamma_HA^*F}_{L^2_T\H}\le a\norm{F}_{L^2_T\H}$.

nodes.name: Factorized pair $(H_0,H)$ with $H=H_0+V_1^*V_2$
nodes.statement: Let $(H_0,H)$ be a pair of self-adjoint operators on $\H$ such that $H=H_0+V_1^*V_2$ in the following sense: \begin{itemize} \item $V_1,V_2$ are densely defined closed operators on $\H$ such that we have continuous embeddings $D(H_0)\subset D(V_1)$, $D(H)\subset D(V_1)$ and $D(H)\subset D(V_2)$. \item $\<Hf,g\>=\<f,H_0g\>+\<V_2f,V_1g\>$ for $f\in D(H)$ and $g\in D(H_0)$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: The perturbation is factorized as $V_1^*V_2$ with domain embeddings and a weak identity linking $H$ and $H_0$.

nodes.name: Dense definedness of $V_1^*,V_2^*$
nodes.statement: Note that, under the above conditions, $V_1^*,V_2^*$ are also densely defined.

nodes.name: Banach couple
nodes.statement: Recall that a couple of two Banach spaces $(\A,\B)$ is said to be a Banach couple if both $\A$ and $\B$ are algebraically and topologically embedded in a Hausdorff topological vector space $\mathcal C$.
nodes.origin_citation: classical interpolation theory (uncited in this paper)
differentia: both $\A$ and $\B$ are algebraically and topologically embedded in a Hausdorff topological vector space $\mathcal C$

nodes.name: Proposition 2.3 (abstract perturbation theorem)
nodes.statement:
Let $\A,\B$ be two Banach spaces such that $(\A,\H)$ and $(\B,\H)$ are Banach couples. Suppose that $V_1$ is $H_0$-smooth and $V_2$ is both $H_0$-smooth and $H$-smooth. Consider the following series of estimates:  egin{align} |\<\<e^{-itH_0}\psi,G\>\>_T|&\le s_1
orm{\psi}_{\H}
orm{G}_{L^2_T\B}, \ |\<\<\Gamma_{H_0}F,G\>\>_T|&\le s_2
orm{F}_{L^2_T\A}
orm{G}_{L^2_T\B},\ 
orm{V_1\Gamma_{H_0}^*G}_{L^2_T\H}&\le s_3
orm{G}_{L^2_T\B},\ 
orm{V_1\Gamma_{H_0}F}_{L^2_T\H}&\le s_4
orm{F}_{L^2_T\A},\ 
orm{V_2\Gamma_{H_0}F}_{L^2_T\H}&\le s_5
orm{F}_{L^2_T\A},\ 
orm{V_2e^{-itH}\psi}_{L^2_T\H}&\le s_6
orm{\psi}_{\H},\ 
orm{V_2\Gamma_HV_2^*\wtilde G}_{L^2_T\H}&\le s_7
orm{\wtilde G}_{L^2_T\H}. \end{align} {m (1)} Suppose there exist constants $s_1,s_3,s_6>0$ such that \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_1}, \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_3} and \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_6} are satisfied for all $\psi\in \H$ and simple function $G:[-T,T]	o \H\cap \B$: Then one has $$ |\<\<e^{-itH}\psi,G\>\>_T|\le (s_1+s_3s_6)
orm{\psi}_{\H}
orm{G}_{L^2_T\B} $$ for all $\psi\in \H$ and simple function $G:[-T,T]	o \H\cap \B$. \ {m (2)} Suppose that there exist constants $s_2,s_3,s_4,s_5,s_7>0$ such that \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_2}, \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_3}, \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_4}, \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_5} and \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_7} hold for all simple functions $F:[-T,T]	o \H\cap \A$, $G:[-T,T]	o \H\cap \B$ and $\wtilde G:[-T,T]	o D(H)$. Then one has $$ |\<\<\Gamma_{H}F,G\>\>_T|\le (s_2+s_3s_5+s_3s_4s_7)
orm{F}_{L^2_T\A}
orm{G}_{L^2_T\B} $$ for all simple functions $F:[-T,T]	o \H\cap \A$ and $G:[-T,T]	o \H\cap \B$.
nodes.statement_short: Seven free-operator estimates transfer to the perturbed propagator $e^{-itH}$ and $\Gamma_H$ with explicit constants.
assumptions: Let $\A,\B$ be two Banach spaces such that $(\A,\H)$ and $(\B,\H)$ are Banach couples.
Suppose that $V_1$ is $H_0$-smooth and $V_2$ is both $H_0$-smooth and $H$-smooth.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.3
nodes.statement_short: Duhamel expansion plus Fubini reduces both assertions to the listed free estimates, the inhomogeneous case needing a duality bootstrap for $\norm{V_2\Gamma_HF}$.

nodes.name: Duhamel formula
nodes.statement: We give the proof in detail for the sake of self-containedness. Let us first show the first statement. The Duhamel formula implies \begin{align} \<e^{-itH}\psi,\varphi\>=\<e^{-itH_0}\psi,\varphi\>-i\int_0^t\<V_2e^{-irH}\psi,V_1e^{-i(r-t)H_0}\varphi\>dr,\quad \psi,\varphi\in L^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Write the Duhamel expansion of $\<e^{-itH}\psi,\varphi\>$ around $H_0$.

nodes.name: Pairing, Fubini and the first assertion
nodes.statement: Plugging $\varphi=G(t)$, integrating over $t\in [-T,T]$ and using Fubini's theorem, we learn by the formula \eqref{adjoint_1} of the adjoint $\Gamma_{H_0}^*$ that $$ \<\<e^{-itH}\psi,G\>\>_T=\<\<e^{-itH_0}\psi,G\>\>_T-i\<\<V_2e^{-itH}\psi,V_1\Gamma_{H_0}^*G\>\>_T. $$ Applying \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_1}, \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_3} and \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_6}, we then obtain the first assertion (1).
nodes.statement_short: Pair with $G$, use the adjoint formula, and apply the three hypothesized estimates.

nodes.name: Two Duhamel identities for $\Gamma_H$
nodes.statement_short: Derive the two dual Duhamel identities for $\<\<\Gamma_HF,G\>\>_T$ and bound the first term.

nodes.name: Bootstrap for $\norm{V_2\Gamma_HF}$ and conclusion
nodes.statement:
It remains to deal with $
orm{V_2\Gamma_HF}_{L^2_T\H}=\sup_{
orm{\widetilde G}_{L^2_T\H}=1}|\<\<V_2\Gamma_HF,\widetilde G\>\>_T|$. Since $D(H)$ is dense in $\H$, we may assume $\widetilde G(t)\in D(H)$. Then, taking $D(H)\subset D(V_2^*)$ into account, we use \eqref{proof_proposition_abstract_2_3} with $G=V_2^*\widetilde G$, \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_4}, \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_5} and \eqref{proposition_abstract_2_7} to obtain $ |\<\<V_2\Gamma_HF,\widetilde G\>\>_T|\le (s_5+s_4s_7)
orm{F}_{L^2_T\A} $ which, together with \eqref{proof_proposition_abstract_2_3}, gives us the second assertion. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the remaining term by duality against $\widetilde G\in D(H)$ using the last three estimates.

nodes.name: Notation $2^*$, $2_*$ and $\Gamma_0$
nodes.statement: In what follows we use a standard notation $2^*=2n/(n-2)$, $2_*=2n/(n+2)$. We write $\Gamma_0=\Gamma_{-\Delta}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1 (free Strichartz and weighted estimates)
nodes.statement_short: Endpoint Strichartz estimates for $e^{it\Delta}$ and $\Gamma_0$, plus their $L^{n,\infty}$-weighted consequences.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: \eqref{lemma_proof_1_1} and \eqref{lemma_proof_1_2} are endpoint Strichartz estimates proved by \cite[Theorem 10.1]{KeTa}. The latter two estimates follow from \eqref{lemma_proof_1_2}, H\"older's inequality \eqref{Holder} and the duality.
nodes.statement_short: Quote Keel–Tao for the first two estimates, then deduce the weighted ones by Hölder and duality.

nodes.name: Quote the endpoint Strichartz estimates
nodes.statement: \eqref{lemma_proof_1_1} and \eqref{lemma_proof_1_2} are endpoint Strichartz estimates proved by \cite[Theorem 10.1]{KeTa}.
nodes.statement_short: The first two estimates are Keel–Tao's endpoint Strichartz estimates.

nodes.name: Weighted estimates by Hölder and duality
nodes.statement: The latter two estimates follow from \eqref{lemma_proof_1_2}, H\"older's inequality \eqref{Holder} and the duality.
nodes.statement_short: Insert the $L^{n,\infty}$ weight via Lorentz Hölder, then dualize.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.2 (weighted smoothing estimates for the free evolution)
nodes.statement_short: A family of weighted half-derivative smoothing estimates for $e^{it\Delta}$, $\Gamma_0$ and $\Gamma_0^*$, uniform in $T$.
assumptions: Let $w\in L^2(\R)$ be as in Theorem \ref{theorem_1}, $\rho>1/2$ and $v\in L^{n,\infty}(\R^n)$.
for all $\psi\in L^2$ and simple function $F:\R\to \S(\R^n)$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement_short: Tensorize the 1-D Kenig–Ponce–Vega estimate through a conical partition of unity and a weighted Mikhlin multiplier theorem, then obtain the remaining estimates by duality, Hölder and bilinear real interpolation.

nodes.name: One-dimensional local smoothing and tensorization
nodes.statement:
Let us first consider \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_1}. When $n=1$, it was proved by \cite{KPV} that $$ \sup_{x\in \R}
orm{|D_x|^{1/2}e^{it\partial_x^2}f}_{L^2(\R_t)}\le C 
orm{f}_{L^2(\R_x)} $$ which, together with the unitarity of $e^{it\Delta_{\widehat{x}_j}}$ in $L^2(\R^{n-1})$, implies $$ 
orm{|D_j|^{1/2} e^{it\Delta}\psi}_{L^\infty_{x_j}L^2_TL^2_{\widehat x_j}} \le C
orm{\psi}_{L^2},\quad j=1,2,...,n, $$ uniformly in $T>0$, where $\widehat x_j=(x_1,...,x_{j-1},x_{j+1},...,x_n)\in \R^{n-1}$ and $D_j=-i\partial_{x_j}$.
nodes.statement_short: Import the 1-D Kenig–Ponce–Vega smoothing estimate and tensorize it in the transverse variables.

nodes.name: Conical partition of unity and weighted multiplier bound
nodes.statement:
\eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_1} then is derived from this estimate as follows. Let $\{C_j(\xi)\}$ be a conical partition of unity on $\R^n$ so that $ I=\sum_{j=1}^n C_j(\xi), $ where $C_j\in C^\infty(\R^n\setminus\{0\})$ such that $\supp C_j\subset\{2|\xi_j|>|\xi|\}$ and $\partial_\xi^\alpha C_j(\xi)=O(|\xi|^{-|\alpha|})$. If we set $ \wtilde C_j(\xi)=C_j(\xi)|\xi|^{1/2}|\xi_j|^{-1/2} $ then $\wtilde C_j$ also satisfies $\partial_\xi^\alpha C_j(\xi)=O(|\xi|^{-|\alpha|})$ and $ |\xi|^{1/2}=\sum_{j=1}^n\wtilde C_j(\xi)|\xi_j|^{1/2}. $ Since $w(|x|)^2$ belongs to the Muckenhoupt $A_2$-class, $\wtilde C_j(D)$ is bounded on a weighted space $L^2(\R^n,w(|x|)^2dx)$ by weighted Mikhlin's multiplier theorem (see \cite{KuWh}). Thus we conclude that  egin{align*} 
orm{w(|x|)|D|^{1/2}e^{it\Delta}\psi}_{L^2_TL^2}^2 &\le \sum_{j=1}^n
orm{w(|x|)\wtilde C_j(D)|D_{j}|^{1/2}e^{it\Delta}\psi}_{L^2_TL^2}^2\ &\le C\sum_{j=1}^n
orm{w(|x|)|D_{j}|^{1/2}e^{it\Delta}\psi}_{L^2_TL^2}^2\ &\le C\sum_{j=1}^n
orm{w}_{L^2(\R)}^2
orm{|D_{j}|^{1/2}e^{it\Delta}\psi}_{L^\infty_{x_j}L^2_TL^2_{\widehat x_j}}^2\ &\le C 
orm{w}_{L^2(\R)}^2
orm{\psi}_{L^2}^2 \end{align*} uniformly in $T>0$, where we used the properties $w(|x|)\le C_jw(x_j)$ and $w\in L^2(\R)$ in the third line.
nodes.statement_short: Split $|\xi|^{1/2}$ conically and use the $A_2$ weighted Mikhlin multiplier theorem to sum the directional estimates.

nodes.name: Reduction of the inhomogeneous estimate
nodes.statement: Next, by the same argument as above, \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_2} follows from the following estimate \begin{align*} \norm{|D_j|^{1/2}\Gamma_0 F}_{L^\infty_{x_j}L^2_TL^2_{\widehat x_j}} \le C \norm{F}_{L^2_TL^{2_*,2}}. \end{align*} which is a slight generalization of \cite[Lemma 4]{IoKe}, in which the same estimate with $L^{2_*,2}$ replaced by $L^{2_*}$ was proved. Although the proof is essentially same as that of \cite[Lemma 4]{IoKe}, we briefly recall its strategy for reader's convenience.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the second estimate to a directional bound generalizing Ionescu–Kenig's lemma.

nodes.name: Reduction to $\wtilde\Gamma_0$ and the $TT^*$ setup
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we may assume $j=1$. Then it suffices to show \begin{align} \sup_{x_1}\norm{|D_j|^{1/2}\wtilde\Gamma_0 F}_{L^2_TL^2_{\widehat x_1}}\le C\norm{F}_{L^2_TL^{2_*,2}}, \end{align} where $\wtilde \Gamma_0 $ is defined by $$ \wtilde \Gamma_0 F(t):=\int_{-\infty}^te^{i(t-s)\Delta}F(s)ds. $$ Indeed, the corresponding estimate for $\Gamma_0 -\wtilde\Gamma_0 $ follows from \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_1} and the dual estimate of \eqref{lemma_proof_1_1}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the retarded operator $\wtilde\Gamma_0$, the difference being handled by the already-proved estimates.

nodes.name: Dyadic decomposition and bilinear real interpolation
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the bilinear form dyadically, use the dispersive kernel bound, and conclude by Keel–Tao's bilinear real interpolation.

nodes.name: Estimates (2.3), (2.5)–(2.7) by duality and specialization
nodes.statement: The estimate \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_3} follows from the dual estimate of \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_2} and H\"older's inequality \eqref{Holder}. For \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_5}, we refer to \cite{Chi}. \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_6} and \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_7} follow from \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_2} and \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_3} since $\<x\>^{-\rho}$ satisfies the condition on $w$ in Theorem \ref{theorem_1}.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain the remaining weighted estimates by duality, by citation to Chihara, and by specializing $w=\<x\>^{-\rho}$.

nodes.name: Decomposition of $\Gamma_0$ for the last estimate
nodes.statement: In order to derive \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_8}, we observe from the formula \eqref{adjoint_1} that $\Gamma_0 $ can be brought to the form \begin{align*} \Gamma_0 F(t)=-\Gamma_0 ^*F(t)\pm\Gamma_0 ^{0}F(t)+\Gamma_0 ^{\mp}F(t) \end{align*} for $\pm t\ge0$, where $$ \Gamma_0 ^{0}F(t)=\int_{-T}^Te^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds,\quad \Gamma_0 ^{\pm}F(t)=\int_0^{\pm T}e^{-i(t-s)H}F(s)ds. $$ Then the desired estimate for $\Gamma_0 ^*$ is nothing but \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_6}; the desired estimates for $\Gamma_0 ^{0}$ and $\Gamma_0 ^{\mp}$ follow from \eqref{lemma_proof_1_1}, the dual estimate of \eqref{lemma_smoothing_2_1} with $w=\<x\>^{-\rho}$ and H\"older's inequality \eqref{Holder}.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\Gamma_0$ into $\Gamma_0^*$ plus two full-interval pieces and estimate each separately.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.3 ($|x|^{-1}$ is $H$-supersmooth)
nodes.statement: Let $n\ge3$ and $V$ satisfy Assumption \ref{assumption_A}. Then $|x|^{-1}$ is $H$-supersmooth.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement_short: Factorize $V=V_1V_2$, verify the hypotheses of the abstract perturbation theorem with $H_0=-\Delta$, and conclude by density and duality.

nodes.name: Factorization $V_1=|x|V$, $V_2=|x|^{-1}$ and domain inclusions
nodes.statement_short: Set up the factorization and check the domain embeddings via Sobolev's inequality in Lorentz spaces.

nodes.name: $\Delta$-smoothness of $V_1$ and $V_2$
nodes.statement: Moreover, \eqref{lemma_proof_1_1} and Proposition \ref{proposition_abstract_1} (1) show that both $V_1$ and $V_2$ are $\Delta$-smooth.
nodes.statement_short: Deduce free smoothness of both factors from the Strichartz estimate and Proposition 2.1(1).

nodes.name: Perturbed smoothing bound for $V_2e^{-itH}$
nodes.statement: On the other hand, Propositions \ref{proposition_abstract_1} and \ref{proposition_smoothing_3} show \begin{align} \norm{V_2e^{-itH}\psi}_{L^2_TL^2}\le C \norm{\psi}_{L^2} \end{align} uniformly in $T>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Propositions 2.1 and 3.3 to bound $\norm{V_2e^{-itH}\psi}_{L^2_TL^2}$.

nodes.name: Application of the abstract perturbation theorem
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\B$ adapted to $w$ and apply Proposition 2.3 with $H_0=-\Delta$.

nodes.name: Conclusion by density and duality
nodes.statement: Then the desired estimate follows from density and duality arguments.
nodes.statement_short: Dualize the pairing bound and pass to the limit by density.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3
nodes.statement_short: Reuse the factorization, add the supersmoothness bound for $V_2\Gamma_HV_2$, and apply the abstract theorem for every admissible pair $(\A,\B)$.

nodes.name: Reuse of the factorization
nodes.statement: We use the same decomposition $V=V_1V_2$ as above.
nodes.statement_short: Keep $V_1=|x|V$, $V_2=|x|^{-1}$ from the previous proof.

nodes.name: Inhomogeneous bound from supersmoothness of $V_2$
nodes.statement: Since $V_2$ is $H$-supersmooth, we learn by Proposition \ref{proposition_abstract_1} and a remark after Lemma \ref{lemma_abstract_2} that \begin{align} \norm{V_2\Gamma_HV_2\wtilde G}_{L^2_TL^2}\le C\norm{\wtilde G}_{L^2_TL^2} \end{align} for all simple function $\wtilde G:\R\to D(V_2)$ with the constant $C$ independent of $T$ and $\wtilde G$.
nodes.statement_short: Derive $\norm{V_2\Gamma_HV_2\wtilde G}_{L^2_TL^2}\le C\norm{\wtilde G}_{L^2_TL^2}$ from supersmoothness.

nodes.name: Application of the abstract theorem for all admissible $(\A,\B)$
nodes.statement_short: Feed the seven free estimates into Proposition 2.3 for every choice of $\A,\B$.

nodes.name: Conclusion by density and the Duhamel formula
nodes.statement: Then the assertion follows from density of simple functions $F:\R\to\S$ in $L^2_T\A$ and $L^2_T\B$ and the formula \eqref{solution}.
nodes.statement_short: Extend by density and rewrite via the mild-solution formula.
